title: Liquids flow and borrow the shape of the vessel
summary: A liquid flows, matches the vessel it is poured into, and keeps a flat or slightly curved top where gravity pulls on it.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says a liquid flows and takes the shape of a container, except that it forms a flat or slightly curved upper surface when acted upon by gravity. Away from gravity, that same section says liquids draw themselves into a sphere. The amount of space a liquid sample fills barely changes if you squeeze it. That steady amount is what separates a pourable liquid from a gas, which gives up its amount of space as well. The sphere without gravity is the textbook's limit on the everyday flat top. The page does not time how fast anything pours.
